clue.text: Hackneyed article about studied piece of music

indicators.note: the article wraps around the other pieces, splitting after its second letter

parts.note: the definite article is the word 'the'
to read a subject is to study it at university
a bar is a short measured section of music

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a worn-out piece by a composer who studied it too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hackneyed' can mean a hired horse, but here it is the adjective for worn-out, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something worn out by overuse, like stale jokes or shabby cloth.

clue.text: Rainbow, for example, seen in Waterloo, south of West End

indicators.note: the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the end of the word West is its last letter
a Waterloo is a crushing defeat, a rout

explanation.surface: A rainbow seen over a London station, south of the theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'south of' puts ROUT below T. Waterloo is a London station and the West End its theatre district, but here Waterloo means a crushing defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow is a species of freshwater game fish, an example of the kind.

clue.text: Like one running when seat is empty, unqualified?

definitions.text: Like one running when seat is empty
definitions.meaning: a racehorse that has thrown its jockey runs on unmounted
a rider is a qualifying clause, so without one a statement is unqualified

explanation.definitionFit: A horse without a jockey is unmounted, and a statement lacking an added proviso clause is unqualified.

clue.text: How characters appear in films, but not plays

definitions.text: How characters appear in films, but not plays

parts.words: How characters appear in films, but not plays
parts.note: the letters F, I, L, M, S run in dictionary order, while P, L, A, Y, S do not

explanation.surface: Cast lists in cinema are ordered one way, unlike theatre programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' are letters, not people in a cast: the letters of FILMS are in A-to-Z order.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters in dictionary order, as in the word films, follow this arrangement.

clue.text: Top actor absorbed by evil villain

indicators.note: the star is taken inside the word for evil

parts.note: bad means wicked or evil
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: A leading man is swallowed up by his wicked character.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter or scoundrel is called this as a term of abuse, a rough synonym.

clue.text: A little bit of rigatoni and a lot of cottage cheese

indicators.note: only the opening pair of letters of the pasta word is kept
most of the word is kept, dropping its last two letters

explanation.surface: A dish mixing a little pasta with plenty of soft curd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little bit of' keeps RI of RIGATONI; 'a lot of' keeps COTTA of COTTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese, so a specific example of the kind.

clue.text: Clean leads for Watson and Sherlock Holmes

indicators.note: the leads, or opening letters, of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: A Holmes story's opening lines need tidying up.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something is to clean it with water, a plain synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Fuss about one son being so long in Mexico

indicators.note: the fuss word goes round the one

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A father makes a fuss about a son who has stayed away too long in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a length of time but is a goodbye, the Spanish word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish farewell is the equivalent of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Leaders in church arranged her chair before closing of university

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order
the closing of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Senior clergy have rearranged her seat before the university's end of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns HER CHAIR into HIERARCH; 'closing of' takes Y from university.
explanation.definitionFit: The ranked clergy of a church, its bishops and archbishops, form its ruling order.

clue.text: Money riskily put in, as alternative cup is organized

indicators.note: organized means arranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Funds invested at risk, as a replacement trophy competition is set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is organized' rearranges ALTERNATIVE CUP; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Investors stake funds in new firms hoping for high returns despite high risk.

clue.text: Die awfully in classic work as tragic hero

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for a work

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doomed protagonist meets a dreadful death in a great masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' king of Thebes is the archetypal tragic protagonist of Greek drama.

clue.text: Scientist shortened European garment

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a chemist is a scientist working with substances

explanation.surface: A lab researcher cuts short an item of continental clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last letter T from CHEMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shift or undergarment worn by women.

clue.text: Bad-tempered woman manager mistreated time after time

parts.note: T again for time, at the other end

indicators.note: mistreated suggests the letters are handled roughly and rearranged

parts.note: T again for time, at the other end

explanation.surface: A shrewish woman keeps mistreating her boss, time and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time after time' reads as 'repeatedly', but it supplies one T on each side of the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing, quarrelsome woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Very good in performance, back in title role

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the assembled letters right to left
the word for very sits inside the word for a performance

parts.note: an act is a single performance on stage
so is an intensifier meaning very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A star returns to give an excellent performance in the leading part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole assembly, not just the performance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera is named after its heroine, so the singer of her part takes the title role.

clue.text: For example, sovereign, king or queen

definitions.meaning: a sovereign is a gold coin, an example of a coin
each is one of the chessmen on the board

explanation.definitionFit: A coin is a piece of money, and chessmen such as kings and queens are pieces.

clue.text: Like country's supporters in group at riot I contained

indicators.note: in signals the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: Nationalist fans are among a crowd held back at a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into GROUP AT RIOT I CONTAINED, which hides the answer from the P of group to the C of contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who love and support their own country are said to be patriotic.

clue.text: Rejected support by detractor — that has a pronounced effect on character

definitions.text: that has a pronounced effect on character

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: aid is help or support
a critic disparages or detracts from something

explanation.surface: Someone turns down help offered by a fault-finder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns AID into DIA. The definition is cryptic: an accent mark changes how a written letter, a character, is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent such as an umlaut alters a letter's sound, which is exactly what this mark does.

clue.text: Working on body image, loves appearing in lace

indicators.note: the loves are placed inside the lace word

parts.note: tatting is a handmade knotted lace
love is zero in tennis, O, so two loves are OO

explanation.surface: Someone needlepoints love hearts into lace for a picture on skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatting is a British-known craft of knotting thread with a shuttle to make lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist inks a picture into the skin, working on the body.

clue.text: Conducted trial without condition — I gave evidence

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the trial word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to conduct a trial of something is to test it
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: Someone who ran an unconditional experiment speaks in the witness box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense of outside it wraps the trial word round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence under oath in court.

clue.text: Person having no faith in area when Democrat's moved to centre

indicators.note: the letter shifts from the end of the word to its middle

parts.note: a field is an area of land or study
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: An unbeliever in a constituency where the Democrat has shifted to the middle ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved to centre' shifts the D of FIELD into its middle, giving FIDEL. 'Democrat's moved' reads as politics, but it means the letter moves.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever, one who rejects a religion, is an infidel.

clue.text: Beginning to draw lots, makes drawings absentmindedly

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

parts.note: oodles means lots, a great amount

explanation.surface: An artist starts sketching plenty, idly scribbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw lots' reads as a lottery, but they are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribble idle shapes while one's mind is elsewhere is this verb.

clue.text: Spiteful about brief legal representative follows

indicators.note: the lawyer's abbreviation comes after the first piece

parts.note: C, for circa, is the usual abbreviation for about
atty is the shortened form of attorney

explanation.surface: A nasty remark about a lawyer who is next in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty remarks are slyly malicious, a common synonym for spiteful.

clue.text: Land in Asia, as I communicated on radio

definitions.meaning: the code word for the letter I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: It is the South Asian nation and the radio code word for the ninth letter.

clue.text: Religious believer, ie fully converted

indicators.note: converted means turned into another form, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: ie written out fully is the Latin id est

explanation.surface: A believer, that is to say one wholly converted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ie fully' is ID EST, rearranged by 'converted'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who believes in a creator God from reason without revealed religion holds a religious belief.

clue.text: Infallible pudding and its eating?

parts.note: a fool is a cold dessert of fruit and cream
from the proverb 'the proof of the pudding is in the eating'

explanation.surface: A dessert whose eating settles every argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a British dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot go wrong, however careless the user, is infallible.

clue.text: Quickly pass a group of taxis, for example

definitions.meaning: as a verb it means to move or pass swiftly

definitions.text: a group of taxis, for example
definitions.meaning: a set of vehicles run by one operator, such as a cab firm

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to flit swiftly by, and the noun is a company's collection of vehicles.

clue.text: Examined in court about a couple of pounds, sang like a canary

indicators.note: the court word goes round the pounds

parts.note: a case examined in court is tried
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two of them

explanation.surface: An informer, heard in court over a small sum, told all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sang like a canary' suggests informing, but here it is literal birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaries warble with rapid alternating notes, which is to trill.

clue.text: In charge within coffee bars forming network

indicators.note: the charge abbreviation is placed inside the coffee

parts.note: a latte is milky espresso coffee

explanation.surface: The person running a coffee bar sets up a network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coffee bars' reads as cafés, but 'bars' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a crisscross framework of strips, bars arranged as a grid.

clue.text: Specify chapter and verse? That's exactly what's needed in church

indicators.note: the needed thing is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
it can mean the very thing, the ideal

explanation.surface: A vicar asks for precise biblical references, just the thing for a service.
explanation.walkthrough: To quote chapter and verse is to give an exact reference, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote a passage by its exact reference is to name it as a source.

clue.text: Escape without corporal punishment? That's illuminating

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the escape surrounds the punishment

parts.note: flight is escape by running away
a lash is a stroke of the whip

explanation.surface: Running away to avoid a flogging — a bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'avoiding', but in its old sense of outside it wraps the escape round the whipping.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery torch gives out light, so it is a thing that lights up its surroundings.
